properties.title: Flood Advisory issued July 23 at 11:47AM MDT until July 23 at 2:45PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Arroyo and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Northwestern Socorro County in central New Mexico...

* WHEN...Until 245 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Rises in small streams and normally dry arroyos.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1146 AM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. This  will cause arroyo and small stream flooding.
Between 1 and 1.5 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 0.25 to 0.75 inches are expected
over the area. This additional rain will result in minor
flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of Northwestern Socorro County.
- Low water crossings along Alamocita Creek and the Rio Salado may
become impassable.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Arroyos, streams, and normally dry rivers can become raging killer
currents in a matter of minutes. Water in arroyos can travel many
miles and take hours to reach your location from upstream rain areas.

properties.title: Special Marine Warning issued July 23 at 12:19PM CDT until July 23 at 1:15PM CDT by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
SMWCRP

The National Weather Service in Corpus Christi has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal waters from Port Aransas to Matagorda Ship Channel out 20
NM...
San Antonio, Mesquite, and Espiritu Santo Bays...

* Until 115 PM CDT.

* At 1219 PM CDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located near Matagorda Island 557, moving west at
15 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can quickly form and capsize boats, damage
vessels and oil rigs, and create suddenly higher waves.
Make sure all on board are in a secure location and
wearing life jackets. Expect wind gusts in excess of 34
knots, suddenly higher waves, frequent lightning, and
heavy downpours.

* Locations impacted include...
Port Oconnor.
properties.instruction:
Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued July 23 at 11:55AM EDT until July 23 at 5:45PM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Nuisance to minor flooding caused by excessive rainfall is
expected.

* WHERE...Southeastern Mecklenburg County in the piedmont of North
Carolina...
Northern Union NC County in the piedmont of North Carolina...

* WHEN...Until 545 PM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding of low-lying areas adjacent to streams
and other poor-drainage areas, including farmland, parks,
greenways, boat-access areas, golf courses, underpasses, and
parking lots.  Isolated, shallow flows over roadways is possible.
A few flood-prone, low-water crossings may become impassible.  A
small culvert washout or two is possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1150 AM EDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain due to training heavy rain showers, which have
produced between 1 and 2 inches of rainfall over the past 45-60
minutes.  Nuisance to minor flooding is expected to begin shortly
in the Advisory area.  Areas of greatest concern include
flood-prone areas from Matthews to Indian Trail to Hemby Bridge,
especially within the Crooked Creek and Goose Creek watersheds.

- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain may exacerbate flooding and may
cause more significant flooding to develop.  If storm-total
rainfall amounts exceeds 3-4 inches over the next 1-2 hours, more
significant flooding may develop and a Flash Flood Warning may be
issued.  Caution is advised near any stream or other vulnerable
area.  Seek higher ground immediately if streams start to rise.
Please have a plan in place should flash flooding develop and do
not hesitate to act.

- Some locations that may experience flooding include...
Matthews, Mint Hill, Indian Trail, Weddington, Stallings,
Unionville, Wesley Chapel, Lake Park, Hemby Bridge, Fairview In
Union County and New Salem.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Stay away or be swept away. River banks and culverts can become
unstable and unsafe.

closed due to high water.

likely place to experience minor flooding. Additional rainfall
amounts of 0.5 to 1.5 inches are expected over the area. This

Cades Cove and Great Smoky Mountains National Park.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

deaths occur in vehicles.

In hilly terrain there are hundreds of low water crossings which are
potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not attempt to cross flooded
roads. Find an alternate route.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. It is important to know where
you are relative to streams, rivers, or creeks which can become
killers in heavy rains. Campers and hikers should avoid streams or
creeks.
